text:
Gavin McKenna's rookie season has become a referendum on his coach. The first overall pick scored the winner against the Islanders on Nov. 23 and still got benched, and by Friday Jim Hiller was addressing that decision in public, per Hockey Patrol. The New York Times ran a piece on what it called "the real problem" with Hiller's deployment of him. Bruce Boudreau questioned it too.

The numbers explain both sides. McKenna is playing just 14 minutes a night, and Toronto gets only 43% of the five-on-five expected goals (chance quality) with him on, worse than without him. But he's producing: 16 points in 27 games, eight on the power play, and 2.54 points per 60 that sits well above the league average. His goals run ahead of his chances (7 on 5.0 expected), while his linemates have finished below theirs.

NHL EDGE has his top speed in the 97th percentile, and he's 18. Our range for his season runs from 38 to 59 points. The thing to watch is minutes: whether Hiller hands him more, and what he does with them.
